attempted_claim: Let S be a Sylow 7-subgroup of G2(7) (|S| = 7^6) with the presentation and characteristic subgroups Q (extraspecial of order 7^5), R = C_S(Z_2(S)), and family W = {W_x = Z(S)<x> : x in S\(Q union R)} of subgroups of order 49 as in Parker-Semeraro Sections 3-4. Let F be the finite classified list of saturated fusion systems F on S with O_7(F) = 1 in Parker-Semeraro Theorem 1.1 / Table 1: the group systems F_S(G2(7)), F_S(M), and the rows F70, F71(j_i), F72(j), F73-F76 (including the 27 exotic members identified in Corollary 1.2), each presented by its Alperin-Goldschmidt data (E_F, Aut_F(E), E in E_F union {S}) with E_F subset of {Q, R} union W. Using only this Alperin data and the associated Linckelmann-Webb (S,S)-characteristic biset Omega_F / p-local double-Burnside characteristic idempotent omega_F (Frobenius reciprocity, table of marks, and transfer/restriction to F-centric normalizers such as N_F(Q), N_F(R), N_F(W)), give an explicit congruence/identity, computable from the automizer tuple alone, which holds iff F is realizable as F_S(G) for some finite G with S in Syl_7(G) -- hence satisfied by F_S(G2(7)) and F_S(M) and violated by the 27 exotic rows -- whose verification does not invoke the classification of finite simple groups used in the existing exoticity proof.
decisive_failure: All CFSG-free tools admitted (characteristic biset/idempotent, table of marks, Frobenius reciprocity, stable elements, local divisibilities) yield necessity only, since they hold for every saturated system by general theorems; sufficiency requires classifying groups with the given Sylow 7-subgroup, which needs CFSG. Full automizer actions were unavailable CFSG-free, and the toy feasibility model cannot substitute for real automizer computation.
